problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=2{t}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=6t-3.$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $p(t)=-3t-2$ onto the subspace spanned by the polynomial $q(t)=t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)=\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(-3t-2){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(-3t-2){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =(-2)\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1 \\  & =0-5 \\  & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),q(t)⟩ & =q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1) \\  & =(t){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(t){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1 \\  & =0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{-5}{1}\cdot t \\  & =-5t.\end{aligned}
$$
